stem:
Diya solves $7x+5=3x+17$ using the form $Ax+B=Cx+D$ with $x=\dfrac{D-B}{A-C}$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $A=5$, $B=7$, $C=17$, $D=3$, matching the four printed numbers from smallest to largest.
Only $A$ and $C$ are used; $B$ and $D$ are left out of the formula.

teacher.key_rationale: Positions give A=7, B=5, C=3, D=17, so x=(17-5)/(7-3)=3. Sorting by size mis-identifies the four numbers. Reversing D-B gives the wrong numerator. Dropping B and D omits half the formula.
